mainTopic: Which steps of the מנחה are מעכב: רב's rule that a repeated step is מעכב, שמואל's view, and the challenges to רב from הגשה and salt.
overview: This amud asks which steps of the מנחה are מעכב, meaning the offering is invalid without them. רב says any step the Torah repeats is מעכב. שמואל says only the גרש and שמן are. The גמרא narrows the dispute: both accept the repetition rule, and they argue only about whether taking the קומץ by hand, without a measuring utensil, is repeated. רב counts a פסוק from the משכן's inauguration as the repetition. שמואל answers that permanent rules (דורות) are not learned from a one-time event (שעה), unless that event is repeated many times, like the gifts of the twelve נשיאים. רב כהנא and רב אסי then challenge רב from הגשה, which seems repeated but is not מעכב. The גמרא answers that the second פסוק teaches where הגשה is done, and a ברייתא works out the exact corner of the מזבח. רב אשי adds that רבי אליעזר holds the whole מזבח stood in the north. Finally רב הונא challenges רב from salt, which is not repeated yet is מעכב. His proof from a ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing line: only groats and oil are indispensable
steps.stepSummary: The earlier discussion ends by stating that only the גרש and שמן are מעכב in the מנחה, and nothing else is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The groats and the oil are indispensable, and nothing else is indispensable.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes an earlier discussion. Its conclusion is that only the גרש and the שמן hold back the מנחה, and no other detail does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the end of a derivation that started before this section. It sets out שמואל's position, which the גמרא is about to discuss directly. Keep the phrase in mind, because it comes back in the next step as שמואל's own words.

keyTerms.meaning: Indispensable. Without them, the offering is invalid.

phrases.english: The groats and oil are indispensable,
and nothing else is indispensable.

steps.triggerLanguage: גֶּרֶשׂ וָשֶׁמֶן מְעַכְּבִין, וְאֵין דָּבָר אַחֵר מְעַכֵּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a derivation from before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only the גרש and שמן are מעכב in the מנחה.

steps.title: The core dispute between רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the main topic. רב says any repeated step of the מנחה is מעכב. שמואל says only גרש and שמן are מעכב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the main topic. רב says: any step of the מנחה that the Torah repeats is repeated only to teach that it is indispensable. שמואל says: groats and oil are indispensable, and nothing else is.
steps.whatsHappening: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is returning to discuss an earlier statement directly. It lays out the disagreement between רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב gives a general rule: when the Torah repeats a step, the repetition shows that the step is מעכב. שמואל gives a narrow rule: only two items, גרש and שמן, are מעכב. At first glance, שמואל seems to ignore רב's repetition rule completely.

keyTerms.meaning: "The matter itself." The גמרא is returning to analyze a statement it quoted earlier.

steps.whyThisMatters: רב's principle, that a repeated step is מעכב, is a general tool for deciding which details of a קרבן are essential.

phrases.english: The matter itself: Rav said:
Every place where [the verse] repeated for you
phrases.notes: "Repeated" means the Torah mentions the same step a second time in another פסוק.

phrases.english: in the Torah [a step of] the meal offering,
it is only to make it indispensable.
And Shmuel said: groats and oil are indispensable,
and nothing else is indispensable.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהֶחְזִיר לְךָ הַכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה מִנְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the dispute behind the line that closed step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: a repeated step of the מנחה is מעכב. שמואל: only גרש and שמן are מעכב.

steps.title: Does שמואל ignore a repeated verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל: would he really say a step is not מעכב even though the Torah repeats it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to שמואל, even though a פסוק repeats a step, it does not make it indispensable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions שמואל's position. It finds it hard to believe that he would ignore a step the Torah repeats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repetition is a strong signal from the Torah that a step is essential. If שמואל truly ignores it, his view seems hard to defend. The challenge pushes the גמרא to reinterpret what the dispute is really about.

phrases.english: And according to Shmuel, even though
the verse repeated it,
it does not make it indispensable for him?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִשְׁמוּאֵל, אַף עַל גַּב דִּתְנָא בֵּיהּ קְרָא לָא מְעַכְּבָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's position from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that nothing besides גרש and שמן is מעכב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A repeated פסוק clearly signals that a step is essential, so ignoring it seems unreasonable.

steps.title: Both agree, but they argue over taking the handful by hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל agrees a repeated step is מעכב. The real dispute is about מלא קומצו and בקומצו, the two phrases for taking the handful.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, wherever a פסוק repeats a step, it is certainly indispensable. Here, they disagree about "his handful" and "with his hand."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא withdraws its earlier understanding. Both רב and שמואל accept the repetition rule. They disagree only about one specific detail: the rule for taking the קומץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute shrinks from a broad disagreement about principle to a narrow one about a single case. The open question is whether the rule about how the קומץ is taken counts as repeated in the Torah. The next step brings the source that explains this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. The גמרא is dropping its earlier assumption.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think שמואל rejects רב's repetition rule. After this answer, both accept it. They argue only about whether this particular detail is really repeated.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, כֹּל הֵיכָא דִּתְנָא בֵּיהּ קְרָא
phrases.english: Rather, anywhere that the verse repeated it,
it is certainly indispensable,
and here, regarding "his handful" and "with his hand,"
they disagree,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כֹּל הֵיכָא דִּתְנָא בֵּיהּ קְרָא וַדַּאי מְעַכְּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3 by redefining the dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the scope of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל rejects the principle that a repeated step is מעכב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both accept the principle. They argue only about whether the rule for the קומץ is repeated.

steps.title: The ברייתא: no measuring utensil for the handful
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the two phrases, מלא קומצו and בקומצו, show the כהן must take the קומץ by hand and not measure it with a utensil.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: "his handful" and "with his hand" teach that one should not make a measuring utensil for the handful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to explain what rule the two phrases teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים together teach that the קומץ must be taken with the כהן's hand, not with a measuring tool. This is the detail רב and שמואל argue about: is this rule repeated, and therefore מעכב?

keyTerms.meaning: The handful of flour the כהן removes from the מנחה
That he should not make a measure

phrases.english: As it is taught: "his handful," "with his hand":
that he should not make a measure for the handful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the rule named in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the קומץ must be taken by hand, without a utensil
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading מלא קומצו (ויקרא 2:2) and בקומצו (ויקרא 6:8)

steps.title: רב: the rule is repeated at the משכן's inauguration
steps.stepSummary: רב holds that the hand rule is repeated in a third פסוק, from אהרן's service: "he filled his hand from it." So it is מעכב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב holds: this too is repeated by a פסוק, as it is written, "And he presented the meal offering and he filled his hand from it."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב's side. He finds another פסוק that repeats the rule of using the hand, so for him the rule is מעכב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, "he filled his hand" counts as a repetition of the requirement to use the hand. By רב's own principle, a repeated step is מעכב, so taking the קומץ with a utensil invalidates the offering.

phrases.aramaic: רַב סָבַר: הָא נָמֵי תְּנָא בֵּיהּ קְרָא,
phrases.english: Rav holds: this too the verse repeated,
as it is written: "And he presented the meal offering
and he filled his hand from it,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 9:17. This is about אהרן's service on the day the משכן was inaugurated.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב סָבַר: הָא נָמֵי תְּנָא בֵּיהּ קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רב's side of the dispute defined in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That the hand rule for the קומץ is repeated, and therefore מעכב

steps.title: שמואל: a one-time event can't teach a permanent rule
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rejects רב's proof. The inauguration of the משכן was a one-time event (שעה), and we do not learn rules for all generations (דורות) from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל: we do not derive rules for all generations from a one-time situation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains שמואל's side. He does not count רב's פסוק as a repetition, because it describes a one-time event.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל agrees with the repetition principle, but he says the inauguration פסוק cannot count as a repetition for permanent law. The two phrases מלא קומצו and בקומצו are needed together just to teach the hand rule, so without the inauguration פסוק nothing repeats it, and it is not מעכב. This fits his statement that only גרש and שמן are מעכב.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רב and שמואל agree that a repeated step of the מנחה is מעכב. They disagree whether taking the קומץ by hand is repeated. רב counts the פסוק from the משכן's inauguration. שמואל holds דורות משעה לא ילפינן: permanent rules are not learned from a one-time event.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle דורות משעה לא ילפינן is a general rule of derivation that appears in many places across ש״ס.

phrases.english: And Shmuel: we do not derive generations from a one-time situation.
phrases.notes: He means permanent rules for every generation can't be learned from that special one-day event.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof רב uses in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב's proof-text as a valid repetition
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק describes a one-time event (שעה), and permanent law (דורות) is not derived from it.

steps.title: Does שמואל really never learn the permanent rule from a one-time event?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a case where שמואל himself learns a permanent rule from the inauguration of the משכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does שמואל really not learn rules for all generations from a one-time event? But a משנה teaches: liquid vessels make liquids holy, and dry measures make dry things holy, but not the other way around. And שמואל said this applies only to measuring vessels. Blood-bowls (מזרקות) do make dry things holy, because the פסוק says about the נשיאים' bowls: 'both of them full of fine flour.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's rejection in step 7. It shows that שמואל himself learns a permanent rule from the one-time gifts of the נשיאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, שמואל said we cannot learn דורות from שעה. But here he uses a פסוק about the משכן's inauguration, the bowls filled with flour, to set a permanent rule: מזרקות make dry things holy. This looks like a contradiction in שמואל's own method.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy measuring vessels made for dry things like flour
Make holy (what is put inside them)
Bowls used in the מקדש, mainly for collecting blood

phrases.english: And does Shmuel not learn rules for all generations from a one-time event?
But didn't we learn in a mishnah:
Vessels for liquids make liquids holy,
and measures for dry things make dry things holy,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין כְּלֵי הַלַּח מְקַדְּשִׁין אֶת הַיָּבֵשׁ,
phrases.english: but vessels for liquids do not make dry things holy,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מִדֹּת יָבֵשׁ מְקַדְּשִׁין אֶת הַלַּח.
phrases.english: and measures for dry things do not make liquids holy.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא מִדּוֹת,
phrases.english: And Shmuel said: They taught this only about measuring vessels,
phrases.notes: He means the measuring vessels for liquids, like wine or oil.

phrases.english: but bowls do make dry things holy,
as it is written: 'Both of them full of fine flour'!
phrases.notes: במדבר 7:13, about the gifts of the נשיאים at the משכן's inauguration.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא יָלֵיף שְׁמוּאֵל דּוֹרוֹת מִשָּׁעָה? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the principle שמואל used in step 7 to reject רב's proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's principle that we do not learn דורות from שעה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל himself learns a permanent law about מזרקות from the one-time offerings of the נשיאים, so he contradicts his own principle.

steps.title: The נשיאים passage is special because it repeats twelve times
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the נשיאים passage is different, because the פסוק is repeated twelve times.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the פסוק is repeated twelve times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל. Normally we don't learn דורות from שעה, but the נשיאים passage is an exception because it repeats twelve times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule stays in place. The Torah repeated the same offering for each of the twelve נשיאים, and that heavy repetition shows the detail is meant to teach a lasting rule. The inauguration of אהרן's service is not repeated like that, so שמואל can still reject רב's proof.

phrases.english: It is different there,
because the verse repeats it twelve times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the case is an exception because of its unusual repetition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל seemed to learn דורות from שעה, against his own principle.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל keeps his principle; only a one-time passage repeated twelve times can teach for all generations.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: we generally do not learn דורות from שעה, except when the Torah repeats the passage many times, like the twelve נשיאים.

steps.title: רב כהנא and רב אסי challenge רב from הגשה
steps.stepSummary: רב's students challenge his rule: הגשה is repeated in the Torah, yet it is not מעכב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא and רב אסי said to רב: But what about הגשה, bringing the מנחה to the מזבח? The Torah repeats it, and yet it is not מעכב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב's rule that a repeated step is מעכב. Two students bring a case that seems to break that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that when the Torah repeats a step, it is מעכב. הגשה is repeated, but the משנה says leaving it out does not ruin the מנחה. So the students argue that רב's rule cannot be fully right.

keyTerms.meaning: Bringing the מנחה to the corner of the מזבח
Holds it back; without it, the offering is not valid

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge is aimed at רב, not שמואל. We are back on רב's rule that repetition makes a step מעכב.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב אַסִּי לְרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Kahana and Rav Asi said to Rav:
But what about bringing the offering to the altar, which the verse repeats,
phrases.notes: The first mention is ויקרא 2:8, 'and he shall bring it to the מזבח.'

phrases.english: and yet it is not indispensable!
phrases.notes: The משנה earlier taught that skipping הגשה does not ruin the מנחה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי הַגָּשָׁה, דִּתְנָא בָּהּ קְרָא, וְלָא מְעַכְּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the דורות/שעה discussion and returns to רב's rule about repeated steps.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that any step the Torah repeats is מעכב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הגשה is repeated in the Torah but is not מעכב, which is a counterexample to רב's rule.

steps.title: Where is הגשה repeated?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the Torah repeats הגשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where does the Torah repeat it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to check the students' claim. It asks where the second mention of הגשה appears, and the next line answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge only works if הגשה really appears twice. So the גמרא first makes sure there is a second פסוק before going further.

phrases.english: Where does it repeat it?
phrases.notes: Literally, 'who repeats it?' He means: which פסוק says it a second time?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the factual basis of the קשיא in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק where הגשה is mentioned a second time.

steps.title: The second mention: 'This is the law of the מנחה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the פסוק in פרשת צו as the repeat of הגשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'This is the law of the מנחה: the sons of אהרן shall bring it near before ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting the second פסוק about bringing the מנחה near. This confirms the challenge against רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'bring it near' (הקרב) in ויקרא 6:7 repeat the הגשה from ויקרא 2:8. So הגשה really is said twice, and the challenge to רב stands for now.

keyTerms.meaning: Bring near; here it means הגשה

phrases.english: As it is written: 'This is the law of the meal offering:

phrases.aramaic: הַקְרֵב אוֹתָהּ בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן לִפְנֵי ה׳״!
phrases.english: the sons of Aaron shall bring it near before the Lord'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הגשה is repeated in ויקרא 6:7, so the challenge to רב stands for now.

steps.title: The second verse teaches the location, not a repeat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק in פרשת צו is not a repetition of הגשה. It comes to fix the place where the מנחה is brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse comes to set a place for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב's rule. The second verse about הגשה is not saying the same thing again; it adds new information about where it is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's rule applies only when the Torah truly repeats a law. Here the second verse has its own job, which is to teach the location. So it does not count as a repetition, and הגשה is not shown to be מעכב.

keyTerms.meaning: To fix or set a place
Bringing the מנחה close to the corner of the altar
Holding back the offering; it is not valid without this step

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying הגשה is unimportant. It is only saying that this second verse is not a 'repeat' for the purposes of רב's rule.

phrases.english: That verse is to fix a place for it
phrases.notes: "That verse" means the פסוק in פרשת צו from the previous step. "It" is the מנחה.

phrases.english: is what it comes for,

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא לִקְבּוֹעַ לָהּ מָקוֹם הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10, using the verse identified in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the verse to a different purpose, so it is not a repetition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse in פרשת צו repeats the מצוה of הגשה, so by רב's rule it should be מעכב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse teaches the location of הגשה, so it is not a true repeat and רב's rule is not affected.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the two phrases point to different sides
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the verse is about location. "לפני ה׳" suggests the west, and "אל פני המזבח" suggests the south. Each phrase holds back the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: "Before ה׳" could mean the west, so the verse says "in front of the altar." "In front of the altar" could mean the south, so the verse says "before ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that this verse deals with the place of הגשה. It also sets up a puzzle, which the next step will solve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two phrases in the same verse pull in different directions. One points west, toward the Sanctuary, and the other points south, toward the front of the altar. Because the ברייתא uses the verse this way, we see that its purpose is to teach the location.

keyTerms.meaning: Before ה׳; here it suggests the western side, facing the Sanctuary
In front of the altar; here it suggests the southern side

phrases.english: As it is taught: "Before the Lord" —
one might think it is on the west side?
So the verse says: "In front of the altar."
If it said only "in front of the altar,"
one might think it is on the south side,
so the verse says "before the Lord."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the תירוץ of step 13 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the verse in פרשת צו teaches the location of הגשה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that reads "לפני ה׳" and "אל פני המזבח" as directions.

steps.title: The answer: the southwest corner
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא settles the clash. The מנחה is brought to the southwest corner, facing the point of the corner, and that is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? He brings it to the southwest corner, opposite the point of the corner, and that is enough for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא solves the puzzle from the last step by choosing a spot that fits both phrases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The southwest corner touches both the west and the south. Standing opposite the point of that corner, the כהן keeps both "לפני ה׳" and "אל פני המזבח."

keyTerms.meaning: How can these be worked out?
The southwest corner of the altar
The point or tip of the corner
And that is enough for him

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the תנא קמא's ruling on the exact spot for הגשה. רבי אליעזר disagrees with it in the next step.

phrases.english: How can this be?
He brings it near at the southwest corner
opposite the point of the corner, and that is enough for him.
phrases.notes: He stands facing the very tip of the corner, so he is at the west and the south at the same time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the tension between the two phrases raised in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a spot that fits both verses.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two phrases seem to demand two different sides of the altar.
steps.terutzMaskana: The southwest corner fits both phrases at once.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's rule for two clashing verses
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר asks whether the כהן may choose the west side or the south side of the corner. He states a rule: when two readings clash, keep the one that lets both verses stand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: Might he bring it to the west side of the corner or to the south side of the corner? You said: whenever there are two verses, one that keeps itself and keeps the other, and one that keeps itself and cancels the other, we drop the one that cancels and hold on to the one that keeps both.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives a different view of the ברייתא. He first lays out a general rule, which he will apply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר does not accept that the כהן has a free choice between the two sides of the corner. He sets up a principle: one reading respects both phrases and the other wipes one phrase out, so we choose the reading that respects both.

keyTerms.meaning: Keeps itself and also keeps the other verse
Keeps itself but cancels the other verse

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general tool for reading verses that seem to clash, not only a rule about the מנחה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
One might think he may bring it on the west side of the corner
or on the south side of the corner?
phrases.notes: He means: maybe the כהן can pick either side, as he likes.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַרְתָּ: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה מוֹצֵא שְׁתֵּי מִקְרָאוֹת,
phrases.english: You said: Any place you find two verses,
one that fulfills itself and fulfills the other,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד מְקַיֵּים עַצְמוֹ וּמְבַטֵּל אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ –
phrases.english: and one that fulfills itself and cancels the other —

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּיחִין אֶת שֶׁמְּקַיֵּים עַצְמוֹ וּמְבַטֵּל חֲבֵירוֹ,
phrases.english: we set aside the one that fulfills itself and cancels the other,

phrases.aramaic: וְתוֹפְשִׂין אֶת שֶׁמְּקַיֵּים עַצְמוֹ וּמְקַיֵּים חֲבֵירוֹ.
phrases.english: and we hold on to the one that fulfills itself and fulfills the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to the תנא קמא's southwest-corner ruling in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When two readings clash, keep the reading that lets both verses stand and drop the one that cancels the other.

steps.title: Why the south side keeps both phrases
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר applies his rule. Reading "לפני ה׳" as the west cancels "אל פני המזבח." Reading "אל פני המזבח" as the south still keeps "לפני ה׳." So the south side of the corner is chosen.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say "before ה׳" means the west, you cancel "in front of the altar," which is the south. If you say "in front of the altar" means the south, you have still kept "before ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר shows how his rule works in this case and why it points to the south side of the corner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the southern reading leaves both phrases standing. So, under his rule, the כהן brings the מנחה on the south side of the corner, not the west side.

keyTerms.meaning: You have kept or fulfilled it

steps.whatToRemember: The verse in פרשת צו teaches where הגשה is done, so it is not a repeat for רב's rule. The תנא קמא says the southwest corner. רבי אליעזר says the south side of the corner, because that reading keeps both phrases.

phrases.english: For when you say "before the Lord" means the west,
you have canceled "in front of the altar," which is the south,
but when you say "in front of the altar" means the south,
you have fulfilled "before the Lord" as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the general rule from step 16 to the two phrases of the verse.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's ruling that the מנחה is brought on the south side of the corner.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Comparing the two readings: the western reading cancels the other phrase, while the southern reading keeps both.

steps.title: If the South Side Is Chosen, Where Is 'Before ה׳'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר's choice of the south side: how is 'לפני ה׳' still kept?
steps.simpleTranslation: And where have you fulfilled it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אליעזר's conclusion. If the כהן brings the מנחה on the south side, how is the phrase 'לפני ה׳' still being kept?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said that choosing the south still keeps 'לפני ה׳'. But 'לפני ה׳' was first understood as the west, the side facing the היכל. So the גמרא wants to know how the south side can also count as 'before ה׳'.

keyTerms.meaning: you have fulfilled it (kept the verse)
before ה׳, the phrase that seemed to point west

phrases.english: And where have you fulfilled it?
phrases.notes: 'It' means the words 'לפני ה׳'. If the מנחה goes on the south side, where are those words kept?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אליעזר's claim in step 17 that the south reading still keeps 'לפני ה׳'.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's claim that choosing the south keeps both verses alive
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'לפני ה׳' was read as the west. Bringing the מנחה on the south side seems to leave that phrase unfulfilled.

steps.title: The Whole Altar Stood in the North
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that this תנא places the entire מזבח in the northern half, so its south side faces the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: This תנא holds that the entire מזבח stood in the north.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question. According to this תנא, the whole מזבח was in the northern half of the courtyard, so its south side was right in the middle, facing the היכל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the מזבח is shifted north, its southern edge lines up with the center of the עזרה, directly in front of the קודש הקדשים. So standing on the south side of the corner is also 'לפני ה׳', and both phrases are kept. This also confirms the earlier point: the פסוק teaches location and is not a repetition of הגשה.

keyTerms.meaning: he holds, he is of the opinion
a sage of the משנה or ברייתא period (here, רבי אליעזר)

steps.whatToRemember: The south side counts as 'לפני ה׳' only because this תנא puts the whole מזבח in the north, so its south side faces the היכל.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
This tanna holds
phrases.notes: 'This תנא' is רבי אליעזר from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: the entire altar stood in the north.
phrases.notes: He means the northern half of the courtyard. That puts the altar's south side right in the middle, facing the היכל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: קָסָבַר הַאי תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the physical setup: the position of the מזבח
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The south side of the מזבח is not in front of the היכל, so 'לפני ה׳' would be lost.
steps.terutzMaskana: This תנא holds the whole מזבח is in the north, so its south side does face the היכל and counts as 'לפני ה׳'.

steps.title: Salt Is Not Repeated, Yet It Is Indispensable
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא challenges רב's rule: salt is never repeated in the פסוק, but it still holds back the קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא objected: But there is salt, which the verse does not repeat, and it is still indispensable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attack on רב's rule that a rite of the מנחה is indispensable only when the פסוק repeats it. רב הונא points to salt as a case that breaks the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said a step is מעכב only if the תורה repeats it. Salt is mentioned without being repeated, yet without salt the קרבן is not valid. That suggests indispensability does not depend on repetition.

keyTerms.meaning: he objected to it, raised a strong challenge
salt, put on the קרבן before it is burned
holds back, is indispensable (without it the offering is not valid)

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new challenge. It is not about the corner of the מזבח anymore. It returns to רב's general rule about which steps are indispensable.

phrases.english: Rav Huna objects to this:
phrases.notes: 'This' is רב's rule that a rite is indispensable only if the verse repeats it.

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי מֶלַח, דְּלָא תְּנָא בֵּיהּ קְרָא,
phrases.english: But there is salt, which the verse does not repeat,
and it is indispensable in it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the הגשה challenge is resolved, a new challenge against רב's rule begins.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that only a repeated rite of the מנחה is indispensable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Salt is not repeated in the פסוק, yet it is indispensable. So repetition cannot be the test.

steps.title: Source That Salt Is Indispensable
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא begins quoting a ברייתא on 'ברית מלח עולם הוא' to prove that salt is indispensable.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: 'It is an everlasting covenant of salt', meaning that there will be...
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא starts bringing his proof that salt is indispensable. The ברייתא's explanation continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To make his challenge work, רב הונא must show that salt really is מעכב. He quotes a ברייתא built on the words 'ברית מלח עולם'. The 'everlasting covenant' language is the basis for treating salt as essential.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
"It is an everlasting covenant of salt" –
that there will be

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind רב הונא's claim in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That salt is indispensable even though it is not repeated
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on במדבר 18:19, 'ברית מלח עולם הוא'
